messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 — GPU autoscaler failed to provision capacity for gpu-pool-us-west-2. Queue growth > 8x baseline, token throttling engaged. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/Autoscale/gpu-autoscale?orgId=1

maya (eng-sre, oncall): paging oncall now. I see queue length ~ 12k requests, average latency spiking to 6s. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'scale limit reached' + some nodes flapping.

jon (runtime): I’m looking at driver logs on recently registered nodes. Seeing repeated CUDA/Xid errors and OOMs, causing the node agent to restart the runtime process. Snippet:```
[2026-03-14T14:05:12Z] nvidia: Xid 13, process 24192, gpu 0
[2026-03-14T14:05:12Z] nvidia: GPU OOM on allocate 512MB kernel
[2026-03-14T14:05:13Z] runtime: kvcache freed, session terminated
```

priya (eng-ml): those Xid 13s usually indicate GPU/driver page fault or OOM at the driver level. If the runtime restarts frequently it reduces effective GPU capacity even though nodes count looks fine.

maya: confirmed — autoscaler sees nodes but many are in 'NotReady' or 'runtime-restarting' state. That explains scale limit reached despite node count.

lin (customer-success): we have a few high-traffic customers reporting model timeouts and some 5xxs. Which customers are impacted?

maya: routing to the incident page for customer impact mapping. Priority: enterprise accounts on dedicated pools first.

alex (product): notify Sales/AE for any active high-value clusters. I'll draft a short status update.

jon: quick mitigation plan: 1) move traffic for smaller customers to cpu-fallback tier for short prompts (reduce GPU load); 2) manually add nodes from reserved-pool-us-west-2; 3) restart nvidia-driver on flapping nodes and cordon them if unstable; 4) escalate driver version rollback if we see correlation.

maya: executing 2 & 3 now. @ops-bot kick off reserved pool attach.

ops-bot: reserved-pool attach initiated by maya. ETA ~ 90s.

maya: manually increased max_nodes temporarily to 240 for the pool to allow reserved nodes to join. Starting rolling restart of runtime on nodes with >5 Xid errors in last 5m. Command:```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.status.conditions[?(@.type==\"Ready\")].status}{"\n"}{end}'
```

jon: while you do that I’m collecting dmesg from one flapping node:```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:03:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.567895] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00) 31, PID=24680.
```
This looks like driver/kernel instability on a subset of hosts. Could be firmware/driver mismatch with recent kernel roll.

priya: for immediate impact reduction we can add a temporary routing rule in the router to prioritize stable regions (us-east-1) and reduce concurrency per-session to limit OOM frequency. Will prepare the routing patch.

maya: reserved nodes are joining — confirmed 8 nodes added from reserved-pool-us-west-2. Queue dropping from 12k -> 7.2k within 3 minutes. Partial relief but still above baseline.

lin: update sent to customers: "We’re observing degraded GPU capacity in us-west-2 due to driver instability. We’ve shifted excess traffic and added reserved capacity. Some requests may see increased latency or CPU-fallback. Working on restoring full capacity."

alex: thumbs up. Keep wording conservative — avoid promising ETA yet.

jon: restarted nvidia-driver on 6 flapping nodes. 3 nodes moved to cordoned state (unschedulable) after repeated Xid/ooms. Those nodes show kernel messages consistent with recent kernel patch: referencing module nvidia 525.x vs kernel 6.2.

maya: autoscaler now respecting cordon marks and stopped trying to re-add from the same host class. Good. Metric: effective GPU capacity (healthy_gpus) rising from 62% -> 84% as restarts finish.

priya: routing patch deployed: reduced per-session concurrency from 16 -> 8 for affected model routes in us-west-2. This lowers chance of per-request OOM spikes.

jon: root cause hypothesis: recent host kernel upgrade combined with driver 525.x introduced instability under concurrent kernel launches; under high steady load this surfaces as Xid 13/31 and causes runtime restarts. Short-term mitigation: pin driver to previous confirmed-stable driver on node image, and add a kexec/rollback path.

maya: can we do a quick rollback to the previous driver on a small canary set of nodes to validate?

jon: yes — I’ll roll back driver to 520.78 on 3 canary nodes and run stress-tests. If stable then we schedule a larger rollback via AMI/daemonset.

ops-bot: deploy job started (driver-rollback-canary). Logs: https://ci/internal/jobs/driver-rollback-canary/2345

maya: while that runs, I’m leaving cordons in place and letting the reserved pool absorb traffic. Monitoring for queue and error regressions.

lin: CS updated affected customers with "we’ve added capacity and applied mitigations, we’ll follow up with a detailed postmortem and timeline for full restoration." Some asked for credits — flagged to billing/ops.

alex: good. make sure we capture timeline and signal for postmortem. assign owners for infra / runtime / customer comms.

jon: canary anti-stress run done on 3 nodes for 15m, no Xid/OOMs observed. Rolling rollback to previous driver kicked off to remaining stable nodes; should finish in ~25m.

maya: queue trending down further: now 1.4k, latency back to ~1.2s median. Marking incident as mitigated for active workloads; still tracking until all nodes are patched/rolled back.

priya: adding a watch to evals to detect quality regressions due to CPU-fallback for small prompts. No regressions expected but will alert if response distribution changes.

lin: sending follow-up note to impacted customers with timeline and next steps.

maya: summary (for postmortem): P1 triggered by effective GPU capacity loss caused by driver/kernel incompatibility -> manifested as Xid/OOM -> runtime restarts -> autoscaler perceived nodes as unhealthy leading to scale limits. Mitigations: reserved-pool attach, cordon unstable nodes, driver rollback canary -> full rollback, routing concurrency reduction, customer comms.

alex: add action item: prevent autoscaler from counting nodes in 'runtime-restarting' state as available; also add immediate detection alert for repeated Xid errors per node.

jon: filed runtime ticket: RUNTIME-1458 "Detect and surface repeated CUDA/Xid errors per node and mark for auto-cordon".

maya: assigning postmortem: maya (lead), jon (runtime), priya (ml), lin (CS). Target doc by EOD tomorrow.

ops-bot: incident status changed -> mitigated. Incident channel will remain open for 2 hours for verification.

lin: thanks team. I’ll follow up on credits/CS escalations.

maya: if anyone notices a regression or new flapping nodes ping here. Otherwise I’ll start the timeline collection. :white_check_mark:
